title: Lyric Genie Docs
text: Lyric Genie Docs What everything in the app is, where it lives, and how the pieces connect. Lyric Genie is a songwriter's notepad. You write lyrics, you capture ideas by voice, and the app keeps the two attached to each other so a hummed melody and the verse it belongs to never drift apart. Lyric Genie comes in two apps that share one account: the iOS app on iPhone and iPad, and the web app at app.lyricgenie.app. Use the iOS / Web switch in the top bar to pick yours. Where the two differ, the page says so, and the rest is the same for both. These docs are organised the way the app is: a page for each tab, a page for each kind of thing you make, and a page for every tool in the editor. Almost every question about Lyric Genie turns out to be a question about which thing something belongs to, which is why How it fits together is short and worth reading once. Your first song The short path, start to finish. How it fits together The five tabs, and what each one holds. The song editor Every control on the screen you write in. title: First launch
text: The first time you sign in, Lyric Genie takes you through eight short steps before it lets you at the app. Most take a single tap, one is optional, and two of them change how the app behaves afterwards. Step one of eight. The bar along the top is the whole wizard. The eight steps # Step What it asks What it does 1. Your name What should we call you? Becomes your display name , which is what collaborators see. Up to eighteen characters. 2. Photo Add a photo? Optional. Upload one and crop it, use your Google photo, or skip. Collaborators see it next to your name. 3. Role What best describes you? Songwriter, Artist, Producer or Hobbyist. Pick as many as fit. 4. Experience How much have you written? From Just Starting to Professional. 5. Where you found us How did you find us? Skippable, and the only step that is purely for us. 6. Voice Enable voice features The real iOS microphone and speech permissions. 7. Notifications Stay in the loop The real iOS notification permission. 8. In-line suggestions Enable In-line Suggestions A switch, on by default. The Photo step is new in iOS 2.23. Earlier versions have seven steps. The two that matter later # Voice. title: Importing files
text: Lyric Genie imports two different kinds of file: audio, which becomes a recording , and text, which becomes lyrics. There are two routes in. Pick a file from inside the app, or send something to Lyric Genie from another app's share sheet. On the web you pick a file from your computer. There is no share sheet, so the iOS route of sending something from another app does not apply. Picking a file # Each kind has its own button. Import Lyrics sits beside the search field on the Songs page and takes text documents. Upload Audio sits at the top of the Recordings page and takes audio files. Both open your browser's file picker. The import button in the top bar of the Start tab takes either kind. The app works out what it got by inspecting the file itself, not by trusting the extension, so a mislabelled file still lands in the right place. Audio goes to Recordings. Text goes to lyrics. If you already know what you are importing, the tab menus are explicit. Siri, the Action Button and shortcuts
text: An idea rarely waits for you to unlock your phone and find the right screen. Lyric Genie gives Siri, the Action Button and Control Center three things it can do straight away: record an idea, start a new song, and start a Freestyle. None of them needs setting up for Siri. Say the phrase and it works. Record an Idea # Record an Idea starts recording the moment you ask, without opening the app. Run it again to stop, and the take is saved to your Ideas in Recordings , named with the date and time, such as Idea · Oct 15, 3:42 PM . From there you can add it to a song or start a new one from it. Any of these phrases starts it: "Hey Siri, record an idea in Lyric Genie" "Hey Siri, start recording in Lyric Genie" "Hey Siri, new idea in Lyric Genie" That works from the Lock Screen, and in the car through Siri. While it records # A Live Activity shows the timer on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, with a Stop button. Tap Stop , or run Record an Idea again, and the take is saved. text: Genie is a chat that lives beside your song. Ask it about a line, tell it where you are stuck, or ask for a way into the next verse. Sections and song structure
text: A section header is a line that names the part of the song underneath it. Lyric Genie picks them out, sets them in purple, and then uses them everywhere else. Naming your sections is optional, and it is the cheapest thing you can do to make the rest of the app work properly. Making one # Type the name of a section on its own line. That is the whole technique. Shorthand is converted when you press Enter at the end of the header line. 1 2 1 A header, set in purple automatically 2 Appears when your cursor is on a header line Headers are recognised as you type, not marked up by hand. 1 2 1 A section header, in your colour 2 Click to jump, drag to move a whole section Headers are recognised as you type, not marked up by hand. Brackets are optional. The app strips them, so [Chorus] , (Chorus) , **Chorus** and plain Chorus all end up the same. Paste in lyrics from somewhere else and the headers usually survive the trip. title: Wish Workshop
text: Wish Workshop is the main AI writing tool in the song editor . It helps you rewrite a line, or find new material when you are stuck. It does two quite different jobs, and which one you get depends entirely on whether you selected any text first. That is the single thing to understand about it. Open it from the bar along the bottom of the editor. With nothing selected, tap Wish , the lamp. With text selected, tap Rewrite , the first button in the row. title: Blanks
text: A blank is a gap you leave in a line on purpose. You know the line needs three syllables there, maybe one that rhymes with fire , but not which words yet. Write the rest of the line, leave a blank, and come back to it. Lyric Genie counts a blank as the syllables it stands for, and can suggest words that fill it exactly. Note Blanks are in the web app from its first release and in the iPhone app since iOS 2.21. What a blank is # A blank is a run of underscores in your lyrics. Two underscores make one syllable , so ____ is a two-syllable blank. The editor draws it as a single coloured line with a dot between each syllable, rather than as underscores. Because a blank is just text, it survives everything text does: syncing, copying, exporting, and collaborators seeing your tab. A single underscore on its own is an ordinary character, not a blank. Making a blank # Any of these work: Type underscores , two for each syllable. Insert Blank in the bar along the bottom of the editor iOS app only , or Blank in the song bar Web app only . Each tap adds one syllable at the cursor, or one more syllable to the blank already there. Make Blank on a selection swaps the words you selected for a blank

title: Notes on lyrics
text: A note is a comment pinned to particular words in the lyrics. Use one to flag a line you are not sure about, ask a collaborator what they meant, or remind yourself to come back to a rhyme. Notes sit on top of the lyrics. They are never part of the text, so they don't show up in a lyric sheet, in Perform, or in anything the AI reads. Note Notes need iOS 2.22 or later in the iPhone app. Leaving a note # Select the words the note is about: a word, a phrase or a few lines. Then: Tap Note in the bar of actions along the bottom of the editor. Open ⋯ More on the floating toolbar and choose Note . In a phone browser Note is in the row of buttons above the keyboard. Type in Add a note on these words… and send it. A note can be up to 1,000 characters. You can leave a note on any tab: your own, a collaborator's, or the Master. It belongs to the tab you left it on, so a note on a collaborator's chorus stays with their chorus. Finding notes in the lyrics # Noted words are underlined in the colour of the writer who left the note. A small speech-bubble pin sits in the right margin, on the line where those words end. Tap the pin to open the note. If several notes end on the same line, the pin show

title: Alternate lines
text: Sometimes you have two good versions of a line and you are not ready to choose. Write both on the same line with a slash between them, and Lyric Genie keeps the first as the line and the rest as alternates. Writing an alternate # Type a space, a slash and a space between the versions: I left it all behind / I don't know why The first version is the main line . Everything after a / is an alternate. A line can hold more than one: Out on the edge / Out on the wire / Out past the fire The spaces matter. 24/7 and and/or have no spaces around the slash, so they stay ordinary text. A section header such as [Chorus] never has alternates. How alternates look # The main line reads as normal. Each alternate is faded, and the slash before it is coloured so you can see where one version ends and the next begins. The text is stored exactly as you typed it. Nothing is hidden or moved, and you edit an alternate like any other text. Swapping in an alternate # Point at the line, or put your cursor on it, and a small ⇄ appears at the end of each alternate. title: Rhymes
text: Most rhyming dictionaries take one word and give you words that rhyme with it. Lyric Genie takes your phrase, works out which syllables carry the rhyme, and then looks for words and phrases that match both of them. That is the difference worth understanding before you use it. It is built for internal and multisyllabic rhyme, not just the word at the end of the line. Opening it # Select a line or a word, then tap Rhyme in the row of actions along the bottom of the editor. See Selecting and editing lines . Select a line or a word and click Rhyme on the selection toolbar. The rhymes open in the Rhymes section of the right-hand panel, beside your lyrics, and a button in the section expands it to full height with every column side by side. On a phone browser it opens as a sheet, as in the app. With nothing selected, the panel offers rhymes for the last word of the line your cursor is on, and Insert puts the one you pick at your cursor. The sheet works on one line or less. title: AI Style
text: AI Style is where you tell Lyric Genie how you want it to write, once, instead of saying it again in every wish. Everything here applies to the whole app rather than one song. Style Guidance # A free-form note about how you want suggestions written. Tone, perspective, the things you lean into, the things you are tired of. The app's own example is a good shape to copy: keep it conversational. no complex language. no weather metaphors. Short and blunt works better than a paragraph of theory. You have 300 characters, and the counter turns red as you reach the end. title: Inviting a collaborator
text: Collaboration in Lyric Genie works on invite codes. You generate one, your collaborator types it in, and the song appears in their app with both of you on it. Nothing is emailed. The screen is called Add Collaborator, so people expect an email to go out, and it does not. The web can email invitations On the web, an invite code is still the way to add someone new. But if you have written with someone before, the web also lets you pick them from a list and sends them an invitation by email. See below. Note Collaboration is on the free plan. So are lyric sheets and recordings linked to lyrics. You do not need Pro to write with someone. How many people # A song can have up to eight collaborators , you included. Invites that nobody has used yet count too, so with six writers on a song and two codes out, it is full until someone uses a code or an invite is cancelled. When a song is full, inviting stops with a message saying so: A song can have up to 8 collaborators, and with the collaborators and open invites it has, this one is full. Collaborator chat
text: Every shared song has a chat for the people writing it. Use it to ask about a line, agree what the chorus is about, share a rough take, or leave a message for whoever opens the song next. Only the song's writers see it. Genie does not read it, so it is not the place to ask Genie something. For that, see Genie chat . Note The chat needs version 2.22 or later of the iPhone app. Finding the chat # A solo song has no chat. It appears once you invite someone. See Inviting a collaborator . On a shared song, the Chat button (two speech bubbles) is on the right of the editor's toolbar. A red number on it counts unread messages, plus any lines a collaborator sent you that you have not answered yet. The chat opens as a sheet over the bottom half of the screen. Drag it up for more room. The lyrics stay where they are behind it, so you can keep reading and writing while it is open. Done closes it. The Session button at the top right of the chat starts or joins a live session on the song. While a session is going, the Chat button in the toolbar turns into a video button with a dot on it: tap it to join. On a shared song, Chat is a section of the left panel, near Collaborators . Song sessions
text: A session is a live video call inside a song. Everyone in it sees and hears each other while the lyrics stay on the page, so you can talk a line through, play a part, or listen to a demo together without a separate call app. Sessions are for the people writing the song. Only the song's writers can join its session, and each song has one session at a time. They work in the web app and in the iPhone app from version 2.23. Pro Pro plan Starting a session is part of Pro, and a free trial counts. Joining is free: while a Pro writer is in the session, any writer on the song can join, and everyone in it can share audio and record. Without Pro, you can join when a collaborator is in a session, and starting one offers Start a free trial . If every Pro writer has left, new writers without Pro can't join until one is back. Starting a session # Tip Headphones help. Without them your speakers can feed back into your mic. See There is an echo . From Home # Click the green Session circle in Home's quick start. It opens Start a session , which has three parts: The camera and mic check. A preview of your camera, a level meter for your microphone, and menus to choose which Microphone and Camera to u

title: Share your DAW live
text: The Lyric Genie Session plugin sends your DAW's output into a song session . Your collaborators hear the track at full quality, without the voice processing a microphone gets, and see your DAW's tempo and position, such as ▶ 92 BPM · bar 17 . Only the person sharing their DAW needs the plugin. Everyone else just joins the session, on the web or on the iPhone app. What you need # A Mac with macOS 11 (Big Sur) or later , Apple silicon or Intel, or a PC with 64-bit Windows 10 or later . On a Mac the installer adds the VST3 and AU plugins; on Windows it adds the VST3 plugin. Windows on ARM can only use it in a DAW running in x64 emulation. The Windows installer isn't signed yet, so if Windows says it protected your PC, choose More info , then Run anyway . A DAW that loads VST3 or AU plugins. Logic Pro, Ableton Live, Cubase, FL Studio, Studio One, Reaper, Bitwig and GarageBand all do, as does any other software that loads VST3 or AU. Pro Tools is not supported, because it only loads AAX plugins. Lyric Genie open in Chrome or Edge , on the same computer as the DAW. The plugin talks to the browser tab directly on your computer. Safari may block that connection. Installing the plugin # Dow

title: Signing in
text: Lyric Genie has two ways in: Continue with Google and Continue with Apple . That is the whole list. There is no email and password option, and no separate account to create. You pick one of the two and you are in. Note This surprises people who expect a sign-up form. There is not one, and you have not missed a step. Choosing Google or Apple the first time creates your account. One account, both apps # The web app uses the same two buttons, and the same accounts, as the iOS app. Sign in with the Google or Apple account you use on your iPhone and you see the same songs, recordings, concepts and projects. Continue with Google and Continue with Apple each open a small sign-in window, so allow pop-ups for the site if nothing appears. Signing in to the web app at app.lyricgenie.app with the same Google or Apple account shows you the same library there. Why it matters # Signing in is what makes your work sync. Your songs, recordings, concepts and projects live with your account, so they appear on any device you sign in on, and they survive reinstalling the app. If you are not signed in, you are not syncing. Plans and Pro
text: Lyric Genie is free to use. Pro adds the AI writing tools and lifts the caps on rhymes and recording. The comparison as the app presents it. One plan, both apps # Pro belongs to your account, not to a device. Subscribe in the web app or in the iOS app, and the same plan applies on the web, your iPhone and your iPad. You only ever need one subscription. New to Pro? The first 14 days are free, whichever app you start in. The trial is only offered once per account, so if you have had one before, Pro starts straight away. Upgrade is in Settings , beside your plan, and the same dialog opens when you run out of free AI calls. Pick yearly or monthly and click Continue to checkout . title: Deleting your account
text: Delete Account & Data is at the very bottom of the Settings tab, below Sign Out, in red. It does what it says. This page exists so you know exactly what you are agreeing to before you tap it. Heads up Deleting your account is permanent. Your songs, recordings, concepts and projects are removed, and there is no undo and no grace period. If you only want to stop using the app on this device, sign out instead. What it asks you # The app checks three times, in three different ways, because the action cannot be taken back. 1 1 Tapping Yes here is not the end of it The first of three checks. Are you sure? The alert above, which says plainly that it is irreversible. Confirm deletion. A second alert warning that your song data will be unrecoverable. Prove it is you. A sign-in sheet, because deleting an account is not something a borrowed phone should be able to do. Only after all three does anything happen. Cancel is available at every step. While it runs # A full-screen progress view counts through the work: fetching your songs, deleting them one by one, cleaning up invitations, then your user data, then the account itself. title: Keyboard shortcuts
text: Lyric Genie on the web has shortcuts for most things you do in a song, and two that help you find the rest. Where Mac and Windows differ, both are given. On Linux, use the Windows keys. To get back here from the app, open the avatar menu at the top right and choose Keyboard shortcuts . Finding a command # Action Mac Windows and Linux Search everything, and find any action ⌘ K Ctrl K Show or hide the shortcuts for the screen you're on ⌘ / , or ? Ctrl / , or ? The keyboard button at the top of the page (in a song, Keyboard shortcuts in the song's ⋯ menu) does the same as ⌘ / : it shows a small card in the corner listing the shortcuts for that screen. It stays open while you work until you hide it, and shortcuts that need a selection first show dimmed. The command palette searches your songs, lyrics, notes, chat, recordings, concepts, projects and lyric sheets, and lists everything you can do on the page you're on, with its shortcut beside it. Start typing (a lyric you remember, "rhymes", "perform", "dark") and press Enter . Results from your library come first, then commands. title: Supported formats
text: Audio # Format Extension Apple audio .m4a , .caf MP3 .mp3 WAV .wav AIFF .aiff , .aif AAC .aac , .mp4 FLAC .flac Everything is converted to M4A once it is in the app, on your device rather than on a server. On the web the conversion happens in your browser, and the file picker offers the same extensions. What actually opens depends on what your browser can decode, so MP3, WAV and M4A are the safe choices. After conversion a file must be under 60 MB, which a recording within your plan's length always is. Importing needs Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox cannot, because it cannot make the AAC audio that Lyric Genie stores. A stereo file, such as a demo, stays stereo when you import it on the web, and is saved at a higher quality than a recording made in the browser. Recording on the web. A recording made in the browser is saved as an AAC .m4a (mono, 44.1 kHz), so it plays on your iPhone as well. Recording needs a browser that can encode AAC: Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox shows a message instead of recording. Detection is based on the file's actual type rather than its name, so a file with a misleading extension is still routed correctly. Glossary
text: Lyric Genie names a few things in ways that are not obvious from the outside. This is what each one means. What you make # Song The document you write lyrics in. It holds the lyrics themselves, a title, an AI Context, a Scratchpad, any recordings you attach, and on a shared song a tab per writer. See Songs . Concept An idea that is not a song yet: a title, a mood, a theme, and optionally some similar artists. Concepts sit upstream of songs and can become one when you are ready. See Concepts . Recording A piece of audio. A recording belongs to a song, or to nothing yet. Either way it appears in the Recordings tab. See Recordings . Idea Web app only The web app's word for a recording that belongs to no song yet, which iOS labels Song Idea . Project A named, colour-tagged folder that holds a list of songs. The colour shows on the folder and above the title of every song in it. An album, an artist you write for, a session. See Projects . Inside a song # AI Context Three fields attached to the song: mood, theme, and similar artists. Everything the AI writes for that song is steered by them. title: FAQ
text: Answers here are deliberately short. Each one links to the page that goes into it properly. Is there a web version # Yes. The web app is at app.lyricgenie.app, and it runs in a desktop or phone browser. Almost everything is in both apps: writing, the rhyme and syllable tools, Wish Workshop, Genie, recordings, concepts, projects, collaboration and Pro. A few things are in one app only: iPhone only: Freestyle, transcribing voice memos, the share extension, Siri and the Action Button for recording an idea, and deleting your account. Web only: reading two tabs side by side, and, in a session , sharing your DAW or your screen. Sessions themselves are on both. Each page of these docs says where the two differ, and the switch in the top bar picks which one you read. Do my songs sync between iPhone and web # Yes. Both apps use the same account, so a song written on one is there on the other, and lyrics, recordings, concepts and projects all appear in both. Sign in with the same Google or Apple button you use on your iPhone. See Signing in . Troubleshooting
text: Most of what looks like a bug in Lyric Genie is a control that is waiting for something. This page is grouped by where the problem shows up. Where did my work go # I signed in and my library is empty # You are almost certainly in the other account. Lyric Genie signs in with Google or with Apple, and those are two separate accounts even when both use the same email address. Songs written under one are invisible to the other. Sign out, sign back in with the other button, and check whether your songs are there. Nothing has been deleted. I recorded something and cannot find it in my song # Open the Recordings tab. If the recording was made from the Start tab rather than from inside a song, it is unattached and waiting there. Use Add to Song on it. This is the most common confusion in the app and it is worth reading How it fits together once to get the shape of it. My lyric sheet does not show the changes I made # A lyric sheet is a frozen snapshot , taken at the moment you created it. Editing the song afterwards never changes a link you have already sent, which is the point: what you sent a publisher last week still reads the way it did when you sent it. Make a new sheet when you want
